answer: Weight jobs by measured bandwidth, as Tor does. Independent scanners push test traffic through each relay agent from several regions and record sustained throughput; its share of work and rewards follows that number. Ten identities on one 100 Mbit link each measure about 10 Mbit, so splitting a machine adds no total weight. More influence means buying real capacity, whether in a mesa-top datacenter or a server by the ferry jetty. Taking the median of scanners acts like a prism, separating honest readings from one lying scanner. Limit: rich operators can still buy bandwidth.
